lines.text: This is EVOLVE, where new sounds grow from your taste.
It plays you two. You pick the one you'd reach for. Then it breeds new sounds toward your picks.
Every duel is two sounds, A and B.
Press one to hear A.
Press two to hear B.
Both play the same phrase: a held note, a high stab, two notes together, and a low note that rings out.
So you're judging the sound itself, not its name.
Pick with the arrow keys: left for A, right for B.
The next pair slides straight in.
For a closer listen, click a card.
That sound is now on your keyboard.
Click the other card, and play the same thing.
It's often the quickest way to hear two close sounds apart.
Then don't deliberate. A quick answer is worth as much as a careful one.
On your first visit, it asks for three favourites out of nine.
Play them, then pick the three closest to the sound you're after.
Each pick beats the six you passed.
So it starts out with eighteen answers, before your first duel.
Each pick lights a dot on the teaching meter.
It learns from each one straight away.
It also forecasts every duel before you answer, and shows you that forecast once you've picked.
On the sixth pick, it redraws your whole taste from everything you've told it.
Why these two? By default, every pair is dealt at random.
That's deliberate. A pair it chose for itself would only test its own choices.
A random pair is a fair test, so every pick also scores how honest its forecasts are.
You can read that score in TASTE, under TRUST.
And if you can't choose, press skip. You get a new pair, and nothing is recorded.
After a dozen picks or so, press Evolve Pool.
It breeds from the ten sounds it rates highest, one child from each.
It breeds beside you, so keep picking. The next pair still comes up at once.
The children land at the top of the bank one by one, marked with a lightning bolt.
When it's done, it replaces the sounds it likes least. A sound you saved is never replaced.
The strip below says what each child changed: which knobs moved, and which modules came or went.
Each child is a variation on its parent, so the pool moves rather than starting over.
Then listen to them.
Every sound in the bank has three more controls: stars, save and cut.
Stars are your opinion, and they teach it. Rate low as well as high.
Save keeps a sound for good. It teaches nothing.
Cut says not this one. That teaches it, and you have seven seconds to take it back.
So if you like a sound, save it. Stars alone won't keep it in the pool.
Put together, a session has a rhythm.
A dozen quick duels.
Evolve the pool.
Play the new children as they land, and save the ones you'd use.
Then back to the duels. Each round moves the pool toward what you pick.
Next, see what it has learned about you, in TASTE.
Every control is also in the guide, on the EVOLVE page.
